findings.evidence: tests/test_e2e.py:1186-1187 reads `if res.returncode != 0: pytest.skip("the models are not installed")`, so every non-zero exit of the child process is a skip. I ran the test against scratch copies of the source with the models installed (unmutated copy: 1 passed). (a) committed source (git archive HEAD): `1 skipped`, reason `the models are not installed` (the cause is a TypeError on the unknown argument relevance). (b) grid direction swapped at pipeline.py:1313 (score_grid(sa, sb)): `1 skipped`. (c) a NameError injected into _add_relevance that only the real 1x2 grid reaches: all new tests read `15 passed, 1 skipped`. A wrong ranking or a score outside [0,1] still fails the test; a crash does not. The existing real-model tests skip on a narrower condition: test_e2e.py:815-817 skips only when a control run also fails, test_e2e.py:1049-1061 skips on a cache lookup. Materiality: a later change that breaks --relevance on the real reranker leaves `make test` green with one more skip, and no other automatic test runs the real score_grid through the relevance path. Remedy (EDIT): skip only when the models are absent (the cache lookup of test_e2e.py:1049-1061, or a stderr that names ModelsNotInstalled / NotInitializedError), and assert returncode == 0 otherwise.
